calls.title: Growthbook <> Cape - Demo
calls.summary: The discussion revolved around GrowthBook's feature flagging and experimentation platform, highlighting its capabilities for controlled rollouts and data-driven insights tailored for web and mobile applications. GrowthBook allows for complex configurations and targeted releases while ensuring safety through programmatic API access and automatic rollback features. Insights from experiments and A/B testing were emphasized for understanding user metrics and segmenting data. Cape's preference for managed deployment options and structured communication was also noted, focusing on privacy compliance and security. Initial testing will occur in development environments to validate infrastructure before proceeding with broader deployment plans.

calls.title: Growthbook <> Cape - POC Scoping
calls.summary: The call focused on scoping a proof of concept (POC) for GrowthBook's feature flagging platform with Cape, addressing mobile team needs for safe deployments, server-side SDK evaluation, and analytics. Key participants were Daniel Wathne (GrowthBook sales), Logan Bates (GrowthBook support), Kense Ning (Cape product lead), and Kelcey Damage (Cape infrastructure/security). Next steps include setting up a shared Slack channel, provisioning a Redshift connection (Kelcey to start Thursday), sharing documentation, and scheduling a separate pricing discussion with Kenzie, with the POC targeting a 4-week timeline.

calls.title: GrowthBook <> Cape - Pricing Discussion
calls.summary: Daniel Wathne (GrowthBook sales) presented a two-part pricing model (platform fee plus per-seat cost) to Kense Ning (Cape’s point person), addressing Cape’s need for a privacy-centric, feature-rich experimentation platform with no usage limits. Key pain points included data privacy and feature set suitability, with GrowthBook positioned as the leading vendor. Next steps: Kense will share the proposed pricing with Nathan (Cape’s head of finance) and explore a potential marketing partnership, while Kelsey works on warehouse setup.

calls.title: Growthbook <> Cape - Pricing Review
calls.summary: Nathan Mayer (Cape, likely finance) discussed Growthbook's pricing model with Daniel Wathne (Growthbook sales rep). The product offers a self-hosted experimentation platform with fixed platform and scalable seat costs (no usage limits), addressing pain points around budget predictability and competitor instability (acquired vendors). Next steps: Daniel will check with Kenzie about increasing initial seats to 25 for a potential seat discount; Nathan will follow up internally.

calls.title: Growthbook <> Cape - Check In
calls.summary: The team has agreed to proceed with contract execution, setting a mid-July initiation aim for a start date around the 15th. Dan Wathne will coordinate with the AWS representative for submission by early next week. Communication channels for onboarding have been established, with Dan as the primary contact, while August and Natasha lead post-sales support. The Proof of Concept (PoC) has been validated, allowing for smooth contract signing and deployment planning. Kense Ning will manage internal updates and align communications with product leadership. Additionally, a dedicated support structure has been integrated to enhance client experiences, including training sessions to facilitate smooth onboarding and mitigate potential challenges.
